metadata.title: Walker Jumpman, Extended
metadata.topic: Extending a Godot platformer: a new character and a branching final zone
metadata.audience: practitioners and makers following the channel's Claude workflows
metadata.note: Gameplay beats are real engine capture driven by scripted keyboard input and are labelled as such on screen. Coverage contract in coverage.json; capture provenance in CAPTURE.md.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — ClaudeComposerAsk. walker mode B00. The prompt is an ILLUSTRATIVE RECONSTRUCTION of the Walker ask for this game, not a historical transcript: this project was extended from an existing starter, not generated from a blank Walker run. No invented build receipts. Liam named in first breath.
beats.narration_text: Namaste — this is Liam, in for Bear. Zhaohui Li took walker-jumpman, Bear's one-jump Godot platformer, and extended it: a character you can actually read at eighteen pixels wide, and a final zone that makes you pick a route. Everything after this card is the real build, played through its own keyboard input.

show.event: composer card fades in on the cream page
greeting 'Namaste, Liam' appears above the composer
the Walker ask types in
send button arms terracotta
three RESULT lines land beneath the card

props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about a one-jump 2D platformer — a courier automaton crossing gaps and spikes, ending in a zone that forks into a fast hazardous road and a slower clean climb — into a playable Godot project.
output: Zone 03 forks at a raised pad.

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW — hesitant writer BLUF. Misconception corrected is the reel's actual one: 'a new game' -> 'an extension of Bear's starter'. Whole phrase is the trigger so the corrected sentence stands alone. lead_silence_s gives the typing a head start; seed fixed for this slug.
beats.narration_text: Not a new game — an extension. The starter's two zones are byte-identical in the level data and still walkable. What changed is who you play as, and where the level stops.

'walker-jumpman-zhaohui-li is a new game:' types, then pauses
'a new game' struck through in terracotta
'an extension of Bear's starter' types in its place
corrected sentence settles before the cut

beats.narration_text: One fixed-height jump. No double jump, six ticks of coyote time, six of buffer. Every landing in this level is authored against that one arc.

beats.role_note: GAMEPLAY EVIDENCE — native 3840x2160 Godot Movie Maker capture, scripted keyboard input, real engine run. Labelled SCRIPTED INPUT on screen. Not a human playtest. Clip is capture/run-01.avi 17.00-30.23s at real speed; any tail beyond the action is a labelled held frame.
beats.narration_text: The other line climbs. A step, then two ledges, no hazard on the route. An early draft stacked these ledges straight over the low road — and the jump underneath clipped them. The body is twenty-eight pixels tall and jumps fifty-six, so it needed eighty-four pixels of headroom and had forty-eight. The fix was geometry, not tuning. The ledge overhangs the finish pad, so the high line ends by falling. Flag, results, Enter, and it replays clean.

show.event: step up, then ledge A, then ledge B — spikes visible below
runs off the last ledge and lands on the finish pad
reaches the relocated flag; results card shows time and retries
Enter replays from zero; P then M returns to the title card

beats.role_note: VERDICT — separates observed working features from what was not shown and what is untested. The focus-loss line is the accepted partial-coverage item; the playtest line is the honest limit of a scripted route.
beats.narration_text: Verdict. Sixteen implemented features shown running, two real deaths and two real recoveries, both fork routes finishing. One implemented feature is not on film: pause on focus loss, which an unattended capture cannot trigger — it is covered by a machine check instead. And this was a scripted route, not a person. It proves the geometry is reachable. It cannot tell you the level is fair.

show.event: verdict artifact page opens on cream
line 1 lands: what ran
line 2 lands: what is not on film
line 3 lands: what a scripted route cannot prove
line 4 lands: the one number that would settle it

artifactLines: Shown running: 16 features, 2 deaths, 2 recoveries, both fork routes finish.
Not on film: pause on focus loss — unattended capture cannot lose focus.
Scripted input proves reachability, not fairness. No human playtest yet.
Untested: the fork-pad take-off window is calculated at ~46 px, never measured.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — Your Turn. The prompt extends this episode's idea into the viewer's own project and is read aloud verbatim, then discussed, before the invitation.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: 'In my Godot platformer, measure the take-off window for every jump the level requires — sweep the jump position frame by frame and report the range that still lands.' That is the number I did not have. It turns is this jump fair into a measurement instead of an opinion. Run it on your own level and see which jump has the narrowest window — that one is where your players will quit.

show.event: composer opens with greeting 'Your turn.'

send button arms terracotta

props.command: In my Godot platformer, measure the take-off window for every jump the level requires: sweep the jump position frame by frame with a scripted input driver and report, for each landing, the range of take-off positions that still land. Flag the narrowest one.
output: Check: is that the jump players quit on?
